questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Look at our National Flag which is also known as tiranga. How many colours are there? Tick ü the correct option.

parts.text: Main How many colours are there?
i Which colour is at the top of the tiranga? white/saffron/green
ii Which colour is below the white colour on the tiranga? pink/saffron/green
iii Which colour is above the green colour on the tiranga? white/saffron/yellow
iv Where is the ashoka chakra on the tiranga? on a corner/in the middle/on a side

markingPoints.description: There are 3 colours; i. saffron; ii. green; iii. white; iv. in the middle

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
There are 3 colours; i. saffron; ii. green; iii. white; iv. in the middle

Working: The Indian National Flag (tiranga) has 3 main colour bands: saffron at the top, white in the middle, and green at the bottom. Below the white band is green, and above the green band is white. The Ashoka Chakra is situated in the middle of the white band.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Who am I?

parts.text: A I am the largest two-digit number.
B I am the largest two-digit number where no digit is repeated.
C I am the smallest two-digit number.
D I am the smallest two-digit number, my digits are repeated.
E I am the smallest two-digit number with 3 at the tens place.
F I am the largest two-digit number with 2 at the ones place.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
A: 99; B: 98; C: 10; D: 11; E: 30; F: 92

Working: Solving each riddle:
A. Two-digit numbers end at 99, so 99 is the largest.
B. The largest two-digit number with distinct digits has 9 in the tens place and 8 in the ones place, which is 98.
C. Two-digit numbers begin at 10, so 10 is the smallest.
D. Two-digit numbers with identical digits are 11, 22, 33... The smallest is 11.
E. Numbers with 3 at the tens place are 30 to 39; the smallest is 30.
F. Numbers with 2 at the ones place are 12, 22, 32... 92; the largest is 92.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Digit swap

parts.text: (a) In the number 1,478, interchanging the digits 7 and 4 gives 1,748. Now, interchange any two digits in the number 1,478 to make a number that is larger than 5,500.
(b)(i) Interchange two digits of 10,593 to make a number between 11,000 and 15,000.
(b)(ii) Interchange two digits of 10,593 to make a number more than 35,000.
(c)(i) Interchange two digits of 48,247 to make a number as small as possible.
(c)(ii) Interchange two digits of 48,247 to make a number as big as possible.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) 7,418 (or 8,471); (b)(i) 13,590; (b)(ii) 50,193 (or 90,513); (c)(i) 28,447; (c)(ii) 84,247

Working: (a) To make a number > 5,500 from 1,478, the thousands digit must be 7 or 8. Swapping 1 and 7 gives 7,418; swapping 1 and 8 gives 8,471.
(b)(i) In 10,593, swapping 0 and 3 gives 13,590, which is between 11,000 and 15,000.
(b)(ii) In 10,593, swapping 1 and 5 gives 50,193 (or swapping 1 and 9 gives 90,513), both greater than 35,000.
(c)(i) To make 48,247 as small as possible, swap the smallest digit 2 with the first digit 4, yielding 28,447.
(c)(ii) To make 48,247 as big as possible, swap the largest digit 8 with the first digit 4, yielding 84,247.

markingPoints.description: For 2 consecutive numbers, all sums are odd; for 3 consecutive numbers, sums alternate between even and odd; for 4 consecutive numbers, all sums are even.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
For 2 consecutive numbers, all sums are odd; for 3 consecutive numbers, sums alternate between even and odd; for 4 consecutive numbers, all sums are even.

Working: For 2 consecutive numbers: 1+2=3, 2+3=5, 3+4=7, 4+5=9. All sums are odd because the sum of an odd and an even number is always odd. For 3 consecutive numbers: 6, 9, 12, 15. The sums alternate between even and odd because sets alternate between having 2 odd numbers and 2 even numbers. For 4 consecutive numbers: 10, 14, 18, 22. All sums are even because 4 consecutive numbers always contain 2 odd numbers and 2 even numbers, and the sum of two odd numbers is even.

questions.stem: Roxie and Estu are estimating 4,63,128 + 4,19,682. Roxie says: 'The sum is near 8,00,000 and is more than 8,00,000.' Estu says: 'The sum is near 9,00,000 and is less than 9,00,000.'

parts.text: (a) Are these estimates correct? Whose estimate is closer to the sum?
(b) Will the sum be greater than 8,50,000 or less than 8,50,000? Why do you think so?
(c) Will the sum be greater than 8,83,128 or less than 8,83,128? Why do you think so?

markingPoints.description: (a) Both estimates are correct; Estu's estimate is closer. (b) Greater than 8,50,000. (c) Less than 8,83,128. (d) 8,82,810.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) Both estimates are correct; Estu's estimate is closer. (b) Greater than 8,50,000. (c) Less than 8,83,128. (d) 8,82,810.

Working: 4,63,128 + 4,19,682 = 8,82,810. (a) Both are correct; Estu's estimate of 9,00,000 is closer (difference is 17,190 vs 82,810). (b) Greater than 8,50,000 because 4,63,128 + 4,00,000 = 8,63,128 > 8,50,000. (c) Less than 8,83,128 because 4,63,128 + 4,20,000 = 8,83,128 and 4,19,682 < 4,20,000. (d) 8,82,810.

questions.stem: Some simplifications are shown below where the letter-numbers are replaced by numbers and the value of the expression is obtained. 1. Observe each of them and identify if there is a mistake. 2. If you think there is a mistake, try to explain what might have gone wrong. 3. Then, correct it and give the value of the expression. 1 If a = – 4, then 10 – a = 6. 2 If d = 6, then 3d = 36. 3 If s = 7, then 3s – 2 = 15. 4 If r = 8, then 2r + 1 = 29. 5 If j = 5, then 2j = 10. 6 If m = –6, then 3 (m + 1) = 19. 7 If f = 3, g = 1 then 2f – 2g = 2. 8 If t = 4, b = 3 then 2t + b = 24. 9 If h = 5, n = 6 then h – (3 – n) = 4.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Correct values: 1. 14; 2. 18; 3. 19; 4. 17; 5. 10 (no mistake); 6. -15; 7. 4; 8. 11; 9. 8

Working: 1. 10 – (-4) = 10 + 4 = 14 (Mistake: subtracted 4 instead of -4).
2. 3d = 3 × 6 = 18 (Mistake: concatenated 3 and 6 to get 36).
3. 3(7) – 2 = 21 – 2 = 19 (Mistake: 3 × 7 - 6 = 15 or calculation error).
4. 2(8) + 1 = 16 + 1 = 17 (Mistake: calculation error).
5. 2(5) = 10 (Correct, no mistake).
6. 3(-6 + 1) = 3(-5) = -15 (Mistake: sign error, got positive 19).
7. 2(3) – 2(1) = 6 – 2 = 4 (Mistake: calculation error, gave 2).
8. 2(4) + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11 (Mistake: concatenated 2 and 4 to 24).
9. 5 – (3 – 6) = 5 – (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8 (Mistake: evaluated 3 - 6 as 1 or sign error).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: 1.3 Angles of Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
questions.stem: ΔABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC and ∠A = 80°. Find the measures of ∠B and ∠C.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
∠B = 50° and ∠C = 50°

Working: In ΔABC, AB = AC.
Since angles opposite to equal sides are equal, ∠B = ∠C.
The sum of angles in a triangle is 180°:
∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°
80° + ∠B + ∠B = 180°
2 × ∠B = 180° - 80° = 100°
∠B = 50°
Since ∠C = ∠B, ∠C = 50°.

questions.stem: Let us try to find a few more pairs of numbers from their sums and differences:

markingPoints.description: (a) 18 and 9 (b) 8 and -4 (c) 5 and -5 (d) -5 and 5 (e) -4 and -3 (f) -10 and 3

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) 18 and 9 (b) 8 and -4 (c) 5 and -5 (d) -5 and 5 (e) -4 and -3 (f) -10 and 3

Working: Let the numbers be x and y. x + y = Sum, x - y = Difference. Adding them gives 2x = Sum + Difference, so x = (Sum + Difference) / 2. Then y = Sum - x.
(a) x = (27 + 9) / 2 = 18, y = 27 - 18 = 9.
(b) x = (4 + 12) / 2 = 8, y = 4 - 8 = -4.
(c) x = (0 + 10) / 2 = 5, y = 0 - 5 = -5.
(d) x = (0 - 10) / 2 = -5, y = 0 - (-5) = 5.
(e) x = (-7 - 1) / 2 = -4, y = -7 - (-4) = -3.
(f) x = (-7 - 13) / 2 = -10, y = -7 - (-10) = 3.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
105

Working: The number of cows must perfectly divide into 3, 5, and 7 groups, so it must be a common multiple of 3, 5, and 7. LCM(3, 5, 7) = 105. The multiples are 105, 210, 315, etc. Since the number is less than 200, it must be 105.

questions.stem: Find the smallest number that is divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 7, but leaves a remainder of 10 when divided by 11.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
2100

Working: The number must be a multiple of LCM(3, 4, 5, 7) = 420. Let the number be 420k. We need 420k to leave a remainder of 10 when divided by 11. 420 divided by 11 gives a remainder of 2, so 420k gives a remainder of 2k. We need 2k to leave a remainder of 10. The smallest positive integer k for this is k = 5. So the number is 420 × 5 = 2100.

questions.stem: Find the LCM of 12 and 15 using prime factorisation.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
60

Working: 12 = 2² × 3. 15 = 3 × 5. LCM contains the maximum occurrences of each prime: 2² × 3 × 5 = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: If the prime factorisation of a number is 2 × 3 and another is 2 × 2 × 5, what is their LCM?

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
60

Working: The maximum occurrences for prime factors are 2² (two 2s), 3 (one 3), and 5 (one 5). LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Two bells ring at intervals of 15 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. If they ring together at 10:00 AM, when will they next ring together? Show your working.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
11:00 AM

Working: The next time they ring together will be given by the LCM of their intervals. LCM of 15 and 20: 15 = 3 × 5, 20 = 2² × 5. LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60 minutes. 60 minutes is 1 hour. So they will ring together 1 hour after 10:00 AM, which is 11:00 AM.

questions.stem: Find the HCF and LCM of 10 and 15 using the efficient procedure (division method).

markingPoints.description: HCF = 5, LCM = 30

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
HCF = 5, LCM = 30

Working: Divide both by the common factor 5. The quotients are 2 and 3, which have no common factors. HCF is the common divisor 5. LCM is the product of the divisor and the remaining quotients: 5 × 2 × 3 = 30.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Patterns, Properties, and a Pretty Procedure!
questions.stem: Verify the relationship HCF × LCM = Product of the numbers for the numbers 24 and 36.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Verified: 12 × 72 = 864 and 24 × 36 = 864.

Working: Prime factorisations: 24 = 2³ × 3, 36 = 2² × 3². HCF = 2² × 3 = 12. LCM = 2³ × 3² = 72. Product of HCF and LCM = 12 × 72 = 864. Product of numbers = 24 × 36 = 864. Since 864 = 864, the relationship is verified.

questions.stem: Find whether 1156 and 2800 are perfect squares using prime factorisation.

markingPoints.description: 1156 is a perfect square; 2800 is not a perfect square.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1156 is a perfect square; 2800 is not a perfect square.

Working: Prime factorisation of 1156 = 2 × 2 × 17 × 17 = (2 × 17)^2 = 34^2. Since all prime factors occur in pairs, 1156 is a perfect square. Prime factorisation of 2800 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 7 = (2^2 × 5)^2 × 7. The factor 7 cannot be paired, so 2800 is not a perfect square.

1 - (vii), 2 - (v), 3 - (i), 4 - (viii), 5 - (ii), 6 - (iii), 7 - (iv), 8 - (vi)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Find the degrees of the following polynomials:

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(i) 2; (ii) 3; (iii) 0; (iv) 1

Working: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable.
(i) In 2x2 – 5x + 3, the highest power of x is 2, so the degree is 2.
(ii) In y3 + 2y – 1, the highest power of y is 3, so the degree is 3.
(iii) –9 is a non-zero constant polynomial (–9 = –9x0), so its degree is 0.
(iv) In 4z – 3, the highest power of z is 1, so the degree is 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: The present age of Salil’s mother is three times Salil’s present age. After 5 years, their ages will add up to 70 years. Find their present ages.

markingPoints.description: Salil's present age is 15 years and his mother's present age is 45 years.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Salil's present age is 15 years and his mother's present age is 45 years.

Working: Let Salil's present age be x years. Then his mother's present age is 3x years.
After 5 years, Salil's age will be x + 5 and his mother's age will be 3x + 5.
According to the problem:
(x + 5) + (3x + 5) = 70
4x + 10 = 70
4x = 60
x = 15.
Salil's present age is 15 years, and his mother's present age is 3 × 15 = 45 years.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: The difference between two positive integers is 63. The ratio of the two integers is 2:5. Find the two integers.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
42 and 105

Working: Let the two positive integers be 2x and 5x.
Their difference is 5x – 2x = 63
3x = 63
x = 21.
Smaller integer = 2 × 21 = 42.
Larger integer = 5 × 21 = 105.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Ruby has 3 times as many two-rupee coins as she has five rupee-coins. If she has a total `88, how many coins does she have of each type?

markingPoints.description: 24 two-rupee coins and 8 five-rupee coins

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
24 two-rupee coins and 8 five-rupee coins

Working: Let the number of five-rupee coins be x.
Then the number of two-rupee coins is 3x.
Total value = 5(x) + 2(3x) = 5x + 6x = 11x rupees.
Given 11x = 88 => x = 8.
Number of five-rupee coins = 8.
Number of two-rupee coins = 3 × 8 = 24.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Shorter piece: 60 feet, longer piece: 240 feet

Working: Let the length of the shorter piece be x feet.
Then the length of the longer piece is 4x feet.
x + 4x = 300
5x = 300
x = 60.
Length of shorter piece = 60 feet.
Length of longer piece = 4 × 60 = 240 feet.

questions.stem: If the length of a rectangle is three more than twice its width and its perimeter is 24 cm, what are the dimensions of the rectangle?

markingPoints.description: Width = 3 cm, length = 9 cm

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Width = 3 cm, length = 9 cm

Working: Let the width of the rectangle be w cm.
Then the length is 2w + 3 cm.
Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2((2w + 3) + w) = 2(3w + 3) = 6w + 6 cm.
Given 6w + 6 = 24
6w = 18
w = 3.
Width = 3 cm.
Length = 2(3) + 3 = 9 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: A positive number is 5 times another number. If 21 is added to both the numbers, then one of the new numbers becomes twice the other new number. What are the numbers?

markingPoints.description: 7 and 35

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
7 and 35

Working: Let the smaller positive number be x. Then the larger number is 5x.
When 21 is added to both, the numbers become x + 21 and 5x + 21.
Since 5x + 21 > x + 21, the larger new number is twice the smaller new number:
5x + 21 = 2(x + 21)
5x + 21 = 2x + 42
3x = 21
x = 7.
The two numbers are 7 and 5 × 7 = 35.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: The digits of a two-digit number differ by 3. If the digits are interchanged, and the resulting number is added to the original number, we get 143. Find both the numbers.

markingPoints.description: 58 and 85

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
58 and 85

Working: Let the tens digit be t and the units digit be u.
Original number = 10t + u, interchanged number = 10u + t.
Sum = (10t + u) + (10u + t) = 11(t + u) = 143 => t + u = 13.
Given |t – u| = 3.
Case 1: t – u = 3.
Adding t + u = 13 and t – u = 3 gives 2t = 16 => t = 8, so u = 5. Original number = 85, interchanged number = 58.
Case 2: u – t = 3.
Adding t + u = 13 and u – t = 3 gives 2u = 16 => u = 8, so t = 5. Original number = 58, interchanged number = 85.
Thus, both numbers are 85 and 58.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Let p(x) = ax + b and q(x) = cx + d be two linear polynomials such that: (i) p(0) = 5. (ii) The polynomial p(x) – q(x) cuts the x-axis at (3, 0). (iii) The sum p(x) + q(x) is equal to 6x + 4 for all real x. Find the polynomials p(x) and q(x).

markingPoints.description: p(x) = 2x + 5 and q(x) = 4x – 1

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
p(x) = 2x + 5 and q(x) = 4x – 1

Working: Let p(x) = ax + b and q(x) = cx + d.
From (i): p(0) = 5 => b = 5.
From (iii): p(x) + q(x) = (a + c)x + (b + d) = 6x + 4 for all x.
Equating coefficients:
a + c = 6 ... (1)
b + d = 4 => 5 + d = 4 => d = –1.
From (ii): p(x) – q(x) cuts the x-axis at (3, 0), so p(3) – q(3) = 0.
(a – c)(3) + (b – d) = 0
3(a – c) + (5 – (–1)) = 0
3(a – c) + 6 = 0
a – c = –2 ... (2)
Adding (1) and (2): 2a = 4 => a = 2.
From (1): 2 + c = 6 => c = 4.
Therefore, p(x) = 2x + 5 and q(x) = 4x – 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Let p(x) = ax + b and q(x) = cx + d be two linear polynomials such that: (i) The graph of p(x) passes through the points (2, 3) and (6, 11). (ii) The graph of q(x) passes through the point (4, –1). (iii) The graph of q(x) is parallel to the graph of p(x). Find the polynomials p(x) and q(x). Also, find the coordinates of the point where these lines meet the x-axis.

markingPoints.description: p(x) = 2x – 1, q(x) = 2x – 9; lines meet the x-axis at (1/2, 0) and (9/2, 0) respectively.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
p(x) = 2x – 1, q(x) = 2x – 9; lines meet the x-axis at (1/2, 0) and (9/2, 0) respectively.

Working: For p(x) = ax + b passing through (2, 3) and (6, 11):
slope a = (11 – 3)/(6 – 2) = 8/4 = 2.
3 = 2(2) + b => b = –1. Thus, p(x) = 2x – 1.
Since q(x) is parallel to p(x), c = a = 2.
q(x) passes through (4, –1): –1 = 2(4) + d => d = –9. Thus, q(x) = 2x – 9.
Intersection with x-axis (y = 0):
For p(x): 2x – 1 = 0 => x = 1/2, point is (1/2, 0).
For q(x): 2x – 9 = 0 => x = 9/2, point is (9/2, 0).

parts.text: 1 “झूरी के साले गया को घर तक गोइ« ले जाने मेें दाँतों पसीना आ गया।”
2 “उसका चेहरा देखकर अंतर्ज्ञान से दोनों मित्रों के दिल काँप उठे।”
3 “झूरी की स्त््री्री ने बैलों को द्ार पर देखा, तो जल उठी।”
5 “आएगा तो दूर ही से खबर लूँगा। देखूँ कैसे ले जाता है।”
6 “जी तोड़कर काम करते हैैं, किसी से लड़ाई-झगड़ा नहीं करते, चार बातेें सुनकर गम खा जाते हैैं।”
7 “अगर वे भी इ«टट का जवाब पत््थथर से देना सीख जाते, तो शशायद सभ्य कहलाने लगते।”
8 “तो फिर वहीं मरो। बंदा तो नौ-दो ग्यारह होता है।”

markingPoints.description:
1. दाँतों पसीना आना: भारी बक्सा छत पर ले जाने में मोहन को दाँतों पसीना आ गया।
2. दिल काँप उठना: भयानक तूफान की आवाज सुनकर बच्चों का दिल काँप उठा।
3. जल उठना: सोहन की तरक्की देखकर पड़ोसी जल उठे।
4. ऐंठकर रह जाना: मालिक की डाँट सुनकर नौकर दिल में ऐंठकर रह गया।
5. खबर लेना: दुष्टों ने गाँव में अशांति फैलाई तो पुलिस ने उनकी अच्छी खबर ली।
6. जी तोड़कर काम करना: परीक्षा में प्रथम आने के लिए उसने जी तोड़कर काम किया; गम खा जाना: बड़ों की डाँट सुनकर समझदार बालक गम खा गया।
7. ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से देना: भारतीय सैनिकों ने शत्रुओं को ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से दिया।
8. नौ-दो ग्यारह होना: पुलिस को देखते ही चोर नौ-दो ग्यारह हो गए।

answerScheme.modelAnswer:

2. दिल काँप उठना: भयानक तूफान की आवाज सुनकर बच्चों का दिल काँप उठा।
3. जल उठना: सोहन की तरक्की देखकर पड़ोसी जल उठे।
4. ऐंठकर रह जाना: मालिक की डाँट सुनकर नौकर दिल में ऐंठकर रह गया।
5. खबर लेना: दुष्टों ने गाँव में अशांति फैलाई तो पुलिस ने उनकी अच्छी खबर ली।
6. जी तोड़कर काम करना: परीक्षा में प्रथम आने के लिए उसने जी तोड़कर काम किया; गम खा जाना: बड़ों की डाँट सुनकर समझदार बालक गम खा गया।
7. ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से देना: भारतीय सैनिकों ने शत्रुओं को ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से दिया।
8. नौ-दो ग्यारह होना: पुलिस को देखते ही चोर नौ-दो ग्यारह हो गए।

Working: वाक्यों में आए मुहावरे और उनके अर्थ:
1. 'दाँतों पसीना आना' - अत्यधिक कठिनाई का सामना करना।
2. 'दिल काँप उठना' - बहुत अधिक डर जाना।
3. 'जल उठना' - ईर्ष्या या अत्यधिक क्रोध होना।
4. 'ऐंठकर रह जाना' - विवश होकर मन मसोस कर रह जाना।
5. 'खबर लेना' - सबक सिखाना या दंड देना।
6. 'जी तोड़कर काम करना' - अत्यधिक परिश्रम करना; 'गम खा जाना' - चुपचाप कष्ट या अपमान सहन कर लेना।
7. 'ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से देना' - कड़ा प्रतिरोध करना।
8. 'नौ-दो ग्यारह होना' - भाग जाना।

questions.stem: ‘मिट््ठू’ शब्द का अर््थ होता है— ममधुरभाषी, ममीठा बोलनेवाला यया तोता। ययह शब्द इतना अधिक प्रचलित है कि इसका प्रययोग एक ममुहावरे मेें भी कियया जाता है— ‘अपने ममुँह मिययाँ मिट््ठू बनना’ जिसका अर््थ है ‘अपनी प्रशंसा आप करना’ यया ‘अपने ममुँह से अपनी बड़ाई करना’। आप कुछ ऐसे ममुहावरों की सूची बनाइए जिनमेें किसी अन््य जीव-जंतु का उल्लेख कियया गयया हो, जैसे नीचे लिखे इस वाक््य मेें है— “अकेले मिट््ठू क््या उड़े, आदर््शवादी जगन ममास्टर के हाथों के सभी तोते उड़ गए।”

markingPoints.description:

2. ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा (ऊँट)
3. भीगी बिल्ली बनना (बिल्ली)
4. बंदर क्या जाने अदरक का स्वाद (बंदर)
5. गधे को बाप बनाना (गधा)

Working: जीव-जंतुओं पर आधारित कुछ प्रमुख मुहावरे और उनके अर्थ:
1. हाथों के तोते उड़ना - होश उड़ जाना / हक्का-बक्का रह जाना।
2. ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा - आवश्यकता से बहुत कम मिलना।
3. भीगी बिल्ली बनना - डरकर सहम जाना।
4. बंदर क्या जाने अदरक का स्वाद - मूर्ख व्यक्ति गुणवान वस्तु का मूल्य नहीं समझता।
5. गधे को बाप बनाना - अपना काम निकालने के लिए मूर्ख की खुशामद करना।

Working: शब्द-युग्मों के अर्थ और वाक्य प्रयोग:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: 2.3 Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Polynomial
questions.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(i) 4x2 – x – 4; (ii) 3x2 – 3√2x + 1; (iii) x2 + √5; (iv) x2 – x + 1; (v) 4x2 + x + 1; (vi) x2 – 4x + 1

Working: A quadratic polynomial with sum of zeroes S and product of zeroes P is given by k(x2 – Sx + P):
(i) S = 1/4, P = –1: x2 – (1/4)x – 1 = (1/4)(4x2 – x – 4). For k = 4, the polynomial is 4x2 – x – 4.
(ii) S = √2, P = 1/3: x2 – √2x + 1/3 = (1/3)(3x2 – 3√2x + 1). For k = 3, the polynomial is 3x2 – 3√2x + 1.
(iii) S = 0, P = √5: x2 – 0x + √5 = x2 + √5.
(iv) S = 1, P = 1: x2 – x + 1.
(v) S = –1/4, P = 1/4: x2 – (–1/4)x + 1/4 = (1/4)(4x2 + x + 1). For k = 4, the polynomial is 4x2 + x + 1.
(vi) S = 4, P = 1: x2 – 4x + 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: 2.2 Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
questions.stem: Find the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = x3 – x2 and state the points where the graph of y = x3 – x2 intersects the x-axis.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Zeroes: 0 and 1; points of intersection: (0, 0) and (1, 0)

Working: p(x) = x3 – x2 = x2(x – 1).
Setting p(x) = 0 gives x2 = 0 or x – 1 = 0, so x = 0 or x = 1.
Therefore, 0 and 1 are the only zeroes of p(x).
The graph intersects the x-axis at the points (0, 0) and (1, 0).

questions.topic: 2.3 Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Polynomial
questions.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum and product of zeroes are –5 and 6, respectively.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
x2 + 5x + 6

Working: Let the quadratic polynomial be ax2 + bx + c and its zeroes be α and β.
We are given α + β = –5 and αβ = 6.
A quadratic polynomial is given by k[x2 – (α + β)x + αβ].
Taking k = 1: x2 – (–5)x + 6 = x2 + 5x + 6.

questions.stem: Metal compound A reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce effervescence. The gas evolved extinguishes a burning candle. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction if one of the compounds formed is calcium chloride.

markingPoints.description: CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l)

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l)

Working: The gas that extinguishes a burning candle and is produced with effervescence is carbon dioxide (CO2). Since calcium chloride (CaCl2) is one of the products, the metal compound A must be a calcium carbonate (CaCO3). The balanced equation is: CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l).

questions.stem: What steps did the French revolutionaries take to create a sense of collective identity among the French people?

markingPoints.description: The ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen) emphasised the notion of a united community enjoying equal rights under a constitution.
A new French tricolour flag was chosen to replace the former royal standard.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
The ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen) emphasised the notion of a united community enjoying equal rights under a constitution.
A new French tricolour flag was chosen to replace the former royal standard.
The Estates General was elected by active citizens and renamed the National Assembly.
Internal customs duties and dues were abolished and a uniform system of weights and measures was adopted.
Regional dialects were discouraged and French, as spoken and written in Paris, became the common language.

evidence.quote: The ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen) emphasised the notion of a united community enjoying equal rights under a constitution.
A new French flag, the tricolour, was chosen to replace the former royal standard.
The Estates General was elected by the body of active citizens and renamed the National Assembly.
Internal customs duties and dues were abolished and a uniform system of weights and measures was adopted.
Regional dialects were discouraged and French, as it was spoken and written in Paris, became the common language of the nation.
